title: Surge buffering, KV prefetch and fast-fail shim to reduce retry amplification during tenant spikes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Several high-severity customer escalations in the last two weeks traced to tenant surge patterns that caused rapid KV cache churn, connection pool contention, and a cascade of retries that produced 5xx waves and timeouts. This ticket implements a three-pronged mitigation: (1) a short in-process surge buffer (token-bucket per-tenant) to smooth incoming request bursts, (2) proactive KV prefetch for hot request prefixes to reduce cache miss amplification during bursts, and (3) a conservative fast-fail shim when inflight per-tenant requests exceed safe thresholds to avoid systemic retry amplification.
acceptance_criteria: New per-tenant surge buffer reduces peak inbound QPS variance by >= 40% in synthetic burst tests
KV prefetch reduces first-token latency P95 on synthetic replay of customer prompt sets by >= 30%
Fast-fail shim prevents retry storms: system-wide 5xx rate does not increase during tenant spike test compared to baseline
End-to-end metrics and dashboard panels added: per-tenant inflight, surge-buffer occupancy, kv-prefetch hit rate, fast-fail count
Integration tests and canary rollout tested in staging and observed for 48h before wide rollout
steps: Instrument current runtime to export per-tenant inflight counts and kv cache miss/hot-prefix metrics (PR #TBD)
Implement in-process token-bucket surge buffer as a small async admission layer with tunable burst and refill parameters (configurable by tenant tier)
Add KV prefetcher: when a request is admitted and matches a hot-prefix heuristic, eagerly warm the KV entry before dispatch
Add fast-fail shim: if inflight > X and last N requests from tenant have timeouts/5xx, return controlled 429/503 with retry-after and guidance to SDK
Expose new metrics to the Console: per-tenant buffer occupancy, prefetch success rate, fast-fail rate; create dashboard and alerts
End-to-end testing: unit + e2e synthetic replay tests, chaos injection for connection pool exhaustion, staging canary rollout to 5% of hosts, monitor 48h
Rollout plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with rollback window and automated health gates
Customer communication: prepare postmortem and guidance for escalated customers if they see initial 429/503 behavior
